Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 96, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-'Alaq

It is Makki.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾. The majority of the people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) hold that this surah is the first surah to be revealed of the Qur'an, and this is narrated from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'isha, and Ibn al-Zubayr.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, that "the first surah to be revealed of the Qur'an was the surah Read in the name of your Lord who..." He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: al-Hakim Abu 'Amr and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Qantari informed us of this hadith; Abu al-Harith 'Ali ibn al-Qasim al-Khattabi informed us; Abu Lubaba Muhammad ibn al-Mahdi informed us; Abu 'Imad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bishr informed us, from [Salama] ibn al-Fadl, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

The report.

And from Jabir: that the first surah to be revealed was the surah al-Muddaththir. [And] we have explained this, and the more correct view is the first view. It is established by the narration of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was begun in revelation was the true dream (al-ru'ya al-sadiqa) during sleep. He would not see a dream except that it came like the break of dawn. Then seclusion (al-khala') became dear to him, so he would go to Hira' and devote himself there for many nights – and this is worship (al-ta'abbud) – and would take provisions for that. Then he would return to Khadija and she would provide for him for the like of it, until the Truth came upon him (fa-ja'ahu) while he was in the cave of Hira'. The angel came to him and said: 'Read!' The Prophet said: 'I said: I am not one who reads.'

He said: So he seized me and pressed me until I reached the limit of exertion, then he released me and said: 'Read!' I said: 'I am not one who reads.' So he seized me and pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of exertion, then he released me and said: 'Read!' I said: 'I am not one who reads.' So he seized me and pressed me a third time until I reached the limit of exertion, then he released me and said: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created... until [He taught man] what he did not know.'"

The report is long and is mentioned in the Two Sahihs.

His saying: ﴿in the name of your Lord﴾ means: read, beginning with the name of your Lord. It was also said: read the name of your Lord, the "ba'" being extra (za'ida); this is what Abu 'Ubayda said, and similar to it is the saying of the poet:

(They are free women, for owners of red veils, black-eyed, who do not recite the surahs.)

Meaning: the surahs, with the "ba'" being extra.

It was also said: read upon the name of your Lord, as one says: "Travel in the name of Allah," meaning upon the name of Allah. The first two views are the well-known ones.

His saying: ﴿who created﴾ means: created mankind.

The passage is short, so I translate it directly.

"And His saying: ﴿He created man from a clinging clot﴾ — meaning: the clot ('alaqah), which is blood. He mentioned it here in the singular form 'alaqah because it is one of the mixed (amshaj) substances, and by it He pointed to what is other than it."

And His saying: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾, meaning: Generous. Among His generosity is that He forbears the sins of His servants and delays their punishment. It is also related from some of them: among His generosity is that the human being worships other than Him, and He does not cut off his provision.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 96, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿Who taught by the pen﴾ means: writing with the pen, and it is a great blessing. Qatadah said: "The pen is a great blessing from Allah; were it not for it, religion would not be established and livelihood would not be set right." Scholars differed regarding the intended meaning of the teaching (ta'lim). One of the two opinions is that it refers to Adam, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and the other opinion is that it refers to every human being who writes with the pen.
And His saying: ﴿He taught man that which he knew not﴾ — we have already explained it, and its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 96, verse 6:

His words: ﴿Nay, indeed man transgresses﴾ were revealed concerning Abu Jahl. It has been reported in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Every nation has a Pharaoh, and the Pharaoh of this nation is Abu Jahl."

This is a gharib (unusual, weak) report.

His words: ﴿Yatgha﴾ mean: he exceeds the limit in disobedience. Al-Kalbi said: Among transgression is that one moves from one station to another in clothing and food.

In some tafsirs: it means that when his wealth increases, he increases his food, his drink, and his clothing (and his mount).

It is also reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: Two insatiable seekers are never satisfied: the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of wealth. They are not equal: the seeker of knowledge seeks the pleasure of the Most Merciful, while the seeker of wealth seeks the pleasure of Satan.
"And His saying: ﴿That he sees himself as self-sufficient﴾ — i.e., he sees himself as rich (ghaniyy)."
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾, i.e., the returning and the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 96, verses 9–10:

And His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?﴾ It is also Abu Jahl. The servant who prays is the Messenger (ﷺ). It is established by the narration of Ibn 'Abbas that Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely step on his neck." It was reported to him that he was praying, so he came to step on his neck, but when he drew near to him he recoiled on his heels. It was said to him: "What is the matter with you, Abu al-Hakam?" He said: "I saw between me and him a trench of fire and wings." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him, limb by limb." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih.

And His saying: ﴿Have you seen﴾ is an expression of wonder directed at the listener. It was also said that its meaning is: "Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays, how can he feel safe from My punishment?" It was also said that its meaning is: "Is he right?" That is, he is not right. In the view of Sibawayh, its meaning is: "Have you seen the one whose deed is this? Tell me about his state in the Hereafter?" And this is an indication that he will come to the punishment of God in the Hereafter.

The Exalted said: ﴿Have you considered, if he is upon guidance or enjoins righteousness?﴾ Meaning: Muhammad.

"And His saying: ﴿Have you seen [the one who] denies and turns away?﴾ — meaning Abu Jahl. The sense is: the one who denies and turns away and forbids a servant when he prays, how can he be like the one who believed in his Lord, was mindful [of Him], and prayed!"

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 96, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Does he not know that Allah sees?﴾ is a threat and a warning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 96, verse 15:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Nay, if he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾. That is: We will surely drag him by his forelock into the Fire. It was also said: We will surely blacken his face. He mentioned the forelock to indicate the face. It was also said: We will surely mark the place of the forelock with blackness, and it suffices with it over the rest of the face.

Linguistically: al-asfa' (the one with the mark) is the wild bull that has blackness on its cheeks. They cited poetry in support of the first opinion:

(A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them, between one who bridles a mare and one who seizes [her] forelock.)

He meant: and he seized his forelock.

And they cited poetry in support of the second opinion:

(And I was, [when] the one of error who lunged at him, [I] marked him on the bridge of his nose with a branding iron.)

He meant: I branded him on his nose.
Its meaning: "a lying, sinful forelock" means that the forelock of its owner is lying and sinful.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So let him call his council (nādiyah)﴾. It is reported that when Abu Jahl denounced the Prophet for his prayer, the Prophet (ﷺ) rebuked him. Abu Jahl said to him: "Do you rebuke me, O Muhammad? By God, there is no one in this valley with more council than I have! I have a more populous assembly and more people!" So God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿So let him call his council﴾, that is, his people by whom he is strengthened, and they are the people of his assembly.

Translation:

"And His saying: ﴿We shall call the guards of Hell (az-zabaniyah)﴾ — they are the angels about whom Allah the Exalted said, describing them: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾. It was also said: they are the helpers of the Angel of Death."

(The singular of az-zabaniyah is zabaniyah according to al-Kisa'i, who said it is zabani; and it is reported from some of them: zaban.)

And His saying: ﴿No! Do not obey him; prostrate yourself and draw near﴾. That is: prostrate yourself to God and draw near to Him through obedience. It was also said: prostrate yourself, O Muhammad, and draw near, O Abu Jahl, so that you may see the punishment of God; and this is a strange (gharib) opinion.
